command: PowerShell here-string containing independent Python probe | python -
probeMethod: Launch actual q001_sqlite_ledger_peer.py in six child processes against separate synthetic databases: three normal and three early-entry mutants.

Hold a raw sqlite3 BEGIN IMMEDIATE in the parent. Read READY, send START_ATTEMPT, receive ATTEMPTING, record perf_counter_ns immediately before parent commit. Parse child ENTERED occurrence time independently of the worker test helper.
Assert entered timestamp is earlier than release-start exactly for mutant runs; normal peers complete after release-start. Child exit codes must be zero.

Construct four version-1 incompatible databases directly with sqlite3: wrong ordinal type and key, composite unique request ID plus hash, partial unique request ID, and nullable request ID. Require ValueError from SqliteLedger for all four.

On a newly initialized valid database, append one event, require same-event retry to return the existing block, require conflicting retry to raise, then inspect raw SQL count and independently recompute SHA256 of sorted-key block JSON.
Recompute exact-byte worker return SHA256 and require the frozen digest. Close every raw connection and child stream and allow the disposable temporary directory to clean up.
initialFindings: P1: worker barrier test passed an injected real child that atomically emitted ATTEMPTING and ENTERED before parent release; observation used parent read order.
P2: a version-1 incompatible schema with ordinal TEXT and composite uniqueness was admitted.

initialAdditionalProbe.exitReason: Assertions completed; reviewer-owned raw sqlite connection prevented initial TemporaryDirectory cleanup on Windows.
initialAdditionalProbe.cleanupDisposition: Exact subsequent cleanup command was blocked by tool policy. Initial synthetic temp residue was disclosed to closer; cleanup not claimed.

claimBoundary: Synthetic single-host candidate proof only. No production cutover, Q001/R0 closure, power-loss durability, retention commitment or final artifact acceptance.
